sources.pantabanganEvidence: The review mentions five Pantabangan Clarias batrachus COI sequences supplied as 'Yambot et al. (unpublished)'. No sequence accession or specimen voucher for those five Pantabangan samples was verified.

crossSourceFindings: The 2006 NAST abstract reports 12 endemic/indigenous taxa in Nueva Ecija, including four freshwater fish; the 2009 Silliman abstract reports ten indigenous plus one endemic taxon in Nueva Ecija. The three author overlap and five named Nueva Ecija waters overlap, so the values are related historical study outputs, not independent richness estimates; methods, taxonomy and survey periods need reconciliation.

The 2026 DNA article abstract exposes only five of its claimed nine species and no verified accession/voucher crosswalk. A third-party-indexed earlier thesis draft reports a different 12-species count and 43 samples, but its status, relationship to the paper and reuse basis are not verified; it is excluded from evidence extraction.
The 2024 largemouth-bass community paper's table and abstract agree on blackchin tilapia being counted in four boats, while its results prose says three. This is a source-internal count conflict.
A separate 2024 largemouth-bass diet paper reports only aggregate prey classes in its accessible abstract; it does not substantiate named prey taxa.

The 2026 DNA paper and 2015 Clarias barcode review both name Apolinario Yambot in connection with Pantabangan barcodes, but shared-project/specimen lineage has not been established; they cannot be treated as independent confirmations.
scopeAndAccuracyLimits: No single reviewed source provides a current, complete Pantabangan fish checklist.
Survey periods, row-level capture locations, catchment/reach geometry and environmental class were not established for all candidate records.
Automated or source-reported names remain unreviewed against current taxonomy and individual specimen evidence.
Historical sampling, stocking, fishery catches, community perceptions and DNA sequences are different evidence types and must remain separate.
No source in this review supports current abundance, catchability, legal status or safety advice.
nextStep: Continue Central Luzon freshwater source review at Paitan Lake and Vaca Dam Reservoir, separating 2021 stocking events from wild/catch records, then broaden the named river, lake, wetland and estuarine inventory. Keep the regional baseline incomplete.
